params.prompt: Traditional Rajasthani Phad scroll painting style, Marwar folk art: flat two-dimensional figure in strict profile, bold black outlines, saturated mineral pigments on aged hand-woven cloth — deep red-ochre ground, indigo, turmeric yellow, white — decorative patterned border on all sides. Album-cover portrait panel: one old lean village bard standing in strict profile at night, singing with his mouth open mid-phrase, eyes closed, deeply weathered face with a white tied beard, large saffron Malwa turban, simple red robe, playing a ravanhatta (spike fiddle) held up with its bow, many thin red sacred threads tied on his bowing wrist, a small oil lamp at his feet, one distant algoza flute hanging at his hip, a rolled painted scroll leaning on the shrine wall behind him, dark indigo star field above. He is paint on cloth, dignified, mid-song. Absolutely no readable text, no letters, no writing, no inscriptions anywhere.
